doc.title: Installation
doc.paragraph: Installing Adaptive Framework, whether to be used for Development or Deployment, can be done in one of many ways. You may choose to build the framework yourself, install the pre-built binaries from a distributive package, or use Docker to run it.

section.title: Using Docker
section.paragraph: Docker is a virtualization tool that can be used to quickly install and use products from pre-built images. To pull the images that have already been built and released, please visit the GitHub project repository for the latest Release links. There are images that can be used to run a production instance of Adaptive Framework and one for demo purposes. There are two additional images, afw-dev-base and afw-base, that are used internally for GitHub workflows, but may also be used to build the first three images from scratch.

row.column: The afwfcgi image provides the FastCGI Service for processing client requests. This image is useful to configure behind a web server such as Apache or Nginx, in order to provide RESTful web services.

The afw-admin image provides nginx and the administrative web app for managing an Adaptive Framework application. This web application is general-purpose and allows you to edit object data as well as configure and maintain services, logs, adapters and authorization handlers.

This image contains everything. It runs both afwfcgi, along with an nginx instance serving the admin interface. Additionally, it has some minimal configuration in place to provide a handful of adapters in order to demo the framework.
This image contains the full development environment needed to build Adaptive Framework. There are multiple distributions supported, including RockyLinux, Ubuntu, Opensuse and Alpine Linux.
This image contains the minimum requirements to run an instance of Adaptive Framework and serves only as a "base" image for the afwfcgi and afw docker images.

section.title: Running Docker Images in Production
section.paragraph: Running the pre-built Docker images in production requires that you have a Docker Engine available. Docker is available for both Desktop and Server environments. For more information, visit:
The chapter describes how to run these images, alone or together under an orchestrator such as Docker Compose.

section.title: Building Docker Images
section.paragraph: If you wish to not to use officially released Docker images, and would like to build your own from scratch, continue with instructions in this section.

The Dockerfiles live under docker/images, one directory per image and one Dockerfile per distribution (for example Dockerfile.alpine and Dockerfile.ubuntu). The order to build them in, with complete commands including multi-architecture builds, is in docker/images/README.md. In short, from the top of the source tree:
section.code:
export OS="alpine"
# 1. Base images: what Adaptive Framework needs to run, and to build. docker build -f docker/images/afw-base/Dockerfile.${OS} \ -t ghcr.io/afw-org/afw-base:${OS} docker/images/afw-base docker build -f docker/images/afw-dev-base/Dockerfile.${OS} \ -t ghcr.io/afw-org/afw-dev-base:${OS} .
# 2. Optional: build the source and copy out installable packages # (.tar, .rpm or .deb, one folder per architecture). docker build -f docker/images/builder/Dockerfile.${OS} -o type=local,dest=. .
# 3. The all-in-one image. docker build -f docker/images/afw/Dockerfile.${OS} \ -t ghcr.io/afw-org/afw:${OS} .
section.paragraph: Alpine Linux is a nice distribution base to use, because it minimizes software packages in order to provide a very compact, secure image.

section.title: Building from Source
section.paragraph: We recommend one of the following platform versions for building from Source:

section.title: Building on Ubuntu 24.04
section.code: # Fetch source for Adaptive Framework git clone https://github.com/afw-org/afw.git

# build tools sudo apt-get install -y cmake pkg-config python3-venv
# libxml2 sudo apt-get install -y libxml2 libxml2-dev
# libicu for Unicode support sudo apt-get install -y libicu-dev
# libunwind and elfutils for stack trace sudo apt-get install -y libunwind-setjmp0-dev elfutils libdw-dev

# LMDB adapter (afw_lmdb) sudo apt-get install -y liblmdb-dev
# LDAP adapter (afw_ldap) sudo apt-get install -y libldap2-dev
# curl functions (afw_curl) and crypto functions (afw_crypto) sudo apt-get install -y libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev
# YAML content type (afw_yaml) sudo apt-get install -y libyaml-dev
# line editing and history in the interactive afw command (optional) sudo apt-get install -y libedit-dev

# FastCGI library sudo apt-get install -y libfcgi-dev
# NGINX sudo apt-get install -y nginx
# debugging sudo apt-get install -y gdb sudo apt-get install -y valgrind sudo apt-get install -y lsof
section.paragraph: afwdev, which builds Adaptive Framework, needs the packages in python-requirements.txt. Ubuntu 24.04 refuses a system-wide pip install, so install them in a virtual environment and keep it on PATH while building:
section.code: sudo apt-get install git cmake pkg-config python3-venv libxml2 libxml2-dev libicu-dev libunwind-setjmp0-dev elfutils libdw-dev liblmdb-dev libldap2-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev libssl-dev libyaml-dev libedit-dev libfcgi-dev nginx git clone https://github.com/afw-org/afw.git python3 -m venv ~/afw-venv && . ~/afw-venv/bin/activate pip install -r afw/python-requirements.txt cd afw ./afwdev build --install
